brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 gathering evites (balloons, potluck, string lights, confetti, open house, fireworks, bunting, picnic, game day, sparkler send-off, winter gathering, summer social).
brief.audience: Anyone hosting anything; neighbours, families, friend groups.
brief.feeling: Warm and welcoming; you can almost hear the evening.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
references: Exploration grid: backyards at blue hour strung with warm string lights, long tables with mismatched chairs, picnic blankets; real and inviting.

proposals.title: The Governed Occasion
proposals.idea: Every card in the set derives its entire visual grammar — spacing, light vector, type axis, particle drift, foil angle — from a single cantus firmus: the geometric measure of a taut string pulled between two fixed points, which shifts per occasion but never negotiates with itself.
proposals.geometry: A vertical golden-section rectangle (1 : 1.618) divided by a single horizontal datum at the lower third — the 'string line' — that is set before any art exists and never moved. Above it: the atmospheric field (sky, light, depth). Below it: the social plane (table, ground, gathering). All foreground cut-outs are anchored to this datum; nothing floats free of it. On-screen at 390 px the datum falls at exactly 241 px from the top, giving the eye a place to rest that is structurally earned, not decorative. The twelve occasions rotate the art plate behind this fixed datum rather than rebuilding the architecture per card.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) for the occasion title: tracked at +80, set in small capitals, placed on the datum line itself so type and structure share a single axis. Lato (OFL) for all live event fields — name, date, venue — in a weight-contrast pair: Lato 300 for labels, Lato 700 for values, both at 14 px minimum. No decorative lettering, no hand-script overlays. The hierarchy is: datum title first, live data second, atmospheric art always behind. Type is never baked; it lives in Tela's text layer and scales with the device's accessible font setting.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific draft-grid prompt returns 12–16 plates in a single cost unit. Prompt directive: 'Twelve dusk-to-blue-hour exterior scenes, each with a single coherent warm light source motivating all shadows — string lights, a fire pit, a sparkler, a lantern — positioned consistently at upper-left at 35 degrees. Photorealistic depth: soft bokeh on a rear plane, sharp social geometry on the middle plane, atmospheric haze on the far plane. Backyards, long tables, picnic blankets, open porches. No people, no faces, no text, no logos. Each plate has a clear lower-third horizon line.' Plates are selected editorially: any plate whose light source does not sit at the declared 35° vector is rejected. The motivated light source then propagates identically into the WebGL foil angle, the bokeh-origin point, and the parallax-tilt offset — so the phone's physical tilt always moves the foreground layer t
proposals.texture: Simulated cold-press paper tooth on the art plate, generated as a procedural normal-map overlay in the WebGL layer (grain frequency 0.4, amplitude 0.06). This is not decorative: it gives the foil shimmer a surface to catch, so the highlight reads as light on a physical object rather than a screen effect. Foil is applied only to the datum line and the occasion title — nowhere else. The restraint is structural: foil marks what holds, not what pleases.
proposals.motion: Three phases, each governed by the datum. Phase 1 — arrival (0–400 ms): the art plate fades from black, the datum line draws left-to-right at a pace of 390 px in 280 ms (constant velocity, no ease-out flourish — a rule arriving, not a performance). Phase 2 — ambient (continuous): foreground cut-outs drift ±4 px on a 6-second sinusoidal cycle, tilt-offset up to ±12 px responding to DeviceOrientation, always resolving back to datum anchor on stillness. Bokeh particles rise at 0.3 px/frame, opacity 0.15 max. Phase 3 — foil pulse (on focus/tap): a single 200 ms highlight sweep along the datum line from left to right, tied to the declared 35° light vector. Reduced-motion: all three phases collapse to a single static render; the datum line is drawn in CSS border, no animation whatsoever. Nothing moves that does not have a structural reason to move.
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1: One Magnific prompt generates 12–16 art plates as a grid (flat cost). Editorial selection: reject any plate failing the 35° light-source test. Step 2: A second Magnific pass generates foreground cut-out elements per occasion — balloons, bunting, sparklers, confetti streams — on transparent fields, same 35° shadow direction, no people. Step 3: WebGL shader (Three.js, Plajah-owned codebase) applies: paper-tooth normal map, foil highlight locked to 35° vector, bokeh particle system originating from light-source position, candle-flicker mask for winter-gathering card only. Step 4: Tela document assembly — art plate as base, cut-outs as tilt-reactive foreground layer, WebGL as effect layer, live text fields as top layer. Step 5: Link-preview thumbnail is a static composite at 1200 × 630 px, datum line visible, no live effects. QR encodes the Tela URL. No physical build, no scan, no co
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial act of rejection: every plate that fails the 35° light-source test is discarded regardless of how beautiful it is. That decision — holding a constraint against a pleasing result — is the human mark. The datum line's exact pixel position (241 px at 390 px width) is a calculated choice, not a default. The foil's confinement to the datum and title, and nowhere else, is a curatorial refusal. These are perceptible signs of making: someone decided what the rule was and enforced it.
proposals.risk: The datum line creates a structural expectation that twelve occasions must all honour — a picnic and a fireworks display share the same lower-third ground plane, which may read as sameness rather than system. The risk is worth it because the alternative — twelve individually composed cards — produces a collection with no legible personality, only variety. A system that can be read twice the same way is more powerful than twelve surprises. If the datum reads as a constraint rather than an architecture, that is a failure of the art plate, not of the rule.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the datum line to arrive with ceremony — a sweep, a glow, a reveal that announces itself. I refuse this. The datum does not perform; it simply is there when the card opens, because a structural element that announces itself has confused ornament for load-bearing. The line draws at constant velocity precisely to deny it drama. If the Dramatist wishes to move the view

proposals.title: Ink Block, Warm Light
proposals.idea: Each evite is a hand-simulated relief print — rough registration, visible ink drag, torn paper edge — lit by a single pre-declared warm source at 28° that the WebGL foil and bokeh must answer to, so the digital shimmer proves the block was carved before the screen touched it.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile bleed. The plate is divided by a coarse off-register grid: three unequal horizontal bands — sky/ceiling (40%), event zone (38%), ground/table (22%) — edges not straight, drifting 2–4px as a mis-pulled print would. Foreground cut-outs (balloons, bunting triangles, sparkler wands, confetti shards) float on the transparent layer and break the band edges intentionally. No centred symmetry; the visual weight sits low-left across all 12.
proposals.typography: Headings: Playfair Display (OFL), set heavy, slightly over-inked — tracking tightened to -0.02em to simulate ink spread. Sub-info: Space Mono (OFL), caps, 11px, tracking +0.15em — reads like a rubber-stamp date line. Event name in Playfair at ~52px, white or deep indigo depending on plate. Live text fields (name, date, venue) sit in a Space Mono block at bottom band, always legible against a semi-opaque ink-wash bar. No script faces; they feel decorative, not material.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific draft grid, 16 plates, single prompt batch: 'twelve celebration scenes — backyard blue hour, long table warm tungsten, picnic blanket dusk, fireworks smoke trail, winter window candle glow, summer garden haze — each rendered as a two-colour relief block print, ink drag visible, registration off by 2–4px, dominant indigo or ochre ink on cream stock, 28-degree motivated warm light from upper-left, no faces, no text, photographic grain at ISO 1600 equivalent, square crop 1024×1024'. Plates are then masked and letterboxed into the portrait band. No photographs of real people; all scenes are generated and printlike.
proposals.texture: Simulated Riso/linocut: ink drag streaks generated as a tiled normal-map overlay (Plajah-owned shader), paper tooth as a high-frequency noise layer at 8% opacity, ink bleed at glyph edges via a CSS mix-blend-mode multiply pass on the type layer. WebGL foil layer is clipped to the torn-edge mask of each plate — shimmer only where the 'ink' sits heaviest, answering the 28° light. Bokeh particles (warm amber, 4–9px) drift up from the ground band at 0.3 opacity.
proposals.motion: Tilt parallax first: foreground cut-outs (balloons, confetti, bunting) drift ±8px on device gyro at 60fps, furthest plane moves most. Then: bokeh particles rise slowly, 18s loop, eased sine. Foil shimmer pulses once on load (0.4s ease-out), then responds only to tilt — it does not loop or flash. Candle/sparkler plates get a 2px flicker offset on the light-leak mask, 0.8s random interval. Reduced-motion: all parallax and particles off; foil is static; only the flicker mask remains as a single opacity breath at 4s interval, imperceptible as animation.
proposals.productionMethod: 1. Single Magnific 16-plate batch from the prompt above; editorial selection of 12 plates — one per theme. 2. Each plate masked into the three-band portrait layout in Tela; torn-edge mask drawn procedurally (Perlin noise on a clipping path, Plajah shader). 3. Foreground cut-out assets (balloon clusters, bunting strings, sparkler wands, confetti) generated as isolated PNG sprites on transparent ground via a second Magnific pass ('single object, white background, relief print style, indigo ink, no shadow'). 4. WebGL layer (Plajah foil shader) applied over plate, clipped to ink-mass mask; bokeh particle system (Plajah JS particle lib) seeded from ground band. 5. Live text fields injected by Tela; Space Mono date/venue bar rendered client-side. 6. Link preview card bakes a static frame at 1200×630 from the plate + heading only.
proposals.humanTrace: The mis-registration drift (2–4px band edges) is not random noise — it is a directional offset consistent with a mis-pulled print pulled bottom-to-top, and it is the same direction across all 12 plates, making it a production fact not a decoration. The ink drag streaks in the normal-map overlay follow the 28° light angle, so the texture and the light are the same committed decision made once before any asset was generated.
proposals.risk: Consumers expect celebration design to be bright, smooth, and immediately legible. This is dark-ground, heavy-ink, intentionally imperfect. The risk is that hosting families read 'rough' as 'cheap' before they read it as 'crafted'. The risk is worth it because the warmth of the blue-hour plates and the amber bokeh carry the emotional register that smooth gradients fake — and because a design that would survive being photocopied four times is a design that was actually made for the material world its guests live in.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the ink drag, the mis-registration, and the bokeh and call what remains honest. I say what remains is inert. The evidence of process — the drag, the offset, the grain — is not decoration; it is the argument that something was committed to before the screen. Remove it and the design has no position on how it was made, which is the same as having no position at all.

proposals.title: Light Source Declares the Party
proposals.idea: Every evite is a single generative contract: one declared polar-coordinate light source per event type propagates every downstream parameter — foil angle, bokeh falloff, parallax gain per depth plane, particle drift vector, shadow offset — so the system behaves differently for each gathering rather than wearing a different costume.
proposals.geometry: Three explicit depth planes per card: background art plate (full bleed, 390px), midground cut-out layer (foreground objects floating 8–14px above plate, tilt-parallax gain ×1.6), foreground particle/bokeh layer (tilt gain ×2.4, closest to viewer). Each plane is a horizontal strip crop — 9:16 portrait — anchored to a golden-ratio horizon line at 61.8% from top, so the text zone always occupies the lower 38.2% regardless of event. Grid logic: 12 cards share one coordinate system; light azimuth rotates clockwise from 0° (winter gathering, top-center cold) to 330° (sparkler send-off, upper-right warm). Azimuth is the only editorial dial; every other parameter is derived.
proposals.typography: Primary: Space Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) — semi-condensed, tracked +20, uppercase event label at 13px sits above a generous 32px event name set in sentence case. Secondary info (date, venue, host) in Space Grotesk Light 14px. No decorative type; the system is the decoration. All live text in Tela, never baked. Reduced-motion fallback collapses parallax and kills particle drift but preserves foil shimmer as a static CSS gradient — legibility is never contingent on motion.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific batch prompt returns a 4×3 grid of 12 art plates in a single pass. Prompt structure: 'Twelve 9:16 backyard-and-gathering scenes at blue hour, each lit by a single motivated warm practical source [source type varies per cell: string lights / sparkler / bonfire / window spill / paper lantern / candle cluster / firework bloom / afternoon sun rake / overcast diffuse / neon sign bounce / christmas fairy light / citronella torch]. Photographic depth of field, film grain at ISO 800 equivalent, no people, set-dressed surfaces only, ultra-detailed, each cell is compositionally distinct, no text.' Plates are editorial selections from that grid — not illustrations, not flat graphics. Each plate is then run through a second Magnific upscale pass with structure preservation at 0.35 to recover grain without sharpening halos. Cut-out foreground objects (balloon cluster, bunting strand, spa
proposals.texture: Grain is structural, not decorative: a WebGL noise pass (simplex, octave 3, scale 0.8) is driven by the same light azimuth parameter, so grain density is highest in shadow quadrant and bleeds toward highlight. Foil shimmer is a two-layer iridescent normal-map shader — base layer is a fixed plate-wide shimmer at the declared azimuth ±8°, reveal layer is unmasked only over metallic event objects (balloon knots, bunting grommets, sparkler rod). No glitter sprites; foil is a material state, not a particle. Bokeh is a depth-of-field shader applied to the background plate only, circle of confusion radius derived from (distance to horizon line) × 0.04.
proposals.motion: Entry sequence is a state machine, not a timeline: Plane 0 (background) fades in over 400ms. Plane 1 (midground cut-outs) translate up 6px over 600ms cubic-ease-out, begin tilt-parallax tracking. Plane 2 (particles/bokeh) resolves last, 800ms, then enters idle drift — slow upward float at 0.3px/frame for light-emitting particles (bokeh, confetti, sparks), zero drift for structural objects (bunting, balloons). Tilt input maps gyroscope X/Y to parallax offset clamped at ±18px per plane; gain is a function of plane index, not a magic number. Candle-flicker shader on relevant plates: a 1D Perlin noise drives opacity on a warm-tinted point light, 8–14Hz, never perfectly periodic. Reduced motion: all translate animations disabled, tilt disabled, particles static, foil shimmer retained as a CSS conic-gradient at fixed azimuth.
proposals.productionMethod: Pass 1 — Magnific batch: 12-cell art plate grid, single prompt, one cost unit. Pass 2 — Magnific upscale: selected plates at 2× with structure 0.35. Pass 3 — Magnific batch: 16-cell foreground object grid (isolated objects, black bg). Foreground extraction: luminance-key shader in WebGL, threshold 0.12, edge feather 2px — no Photoshop. WebGL effects layer: single GLSL fragment shader per card, parameterized by a JSON config object {lightAzimuth, lightElevation, grainDensity, foilObjects[], bokeRadius, particleType}. The config is the only file that differs between all 12 cards; the shader code is shared. Tela handles live text injection, reduced-motion detection, and link-preview OG image rendering (a static rasterize of frame 0).
proposals.humanTrace: The light source declaration is the human act. Choosing that a winter gathering is lit from top-center at a cold 5500K equivalent, versus a sparkler send-off at upper-right 2200K, is an editorial decision that no model makes — it is the director's input that drives the entire system. The grain is film-grain equivalent, not added noise; it is a physical simulation of a photographic process. The foreground object positions within each card are editorially composed — the system does not auto-place; a human selects which cell from the object batch sits where on the horizon line.
proposals.risk: The system risks feeling clinical — twelve cards that are technically coherent but emotionally identical because the rule is too visible. The counter to this is that the light source azimuth produces genuinely different color temperature, shadow direction, and particle behavior per card, and the Magnific plates are photographically distinct scenes, not variations on a template. The deeper risk is that the shader complexity exceeds mobile GPU budget on mid-range Android. Mitigation: the foil layer degrades to a CSS conic-gradient, the grain pass drops to a static PNG overlay, and the parallax gain halves — declared in the config, not hacked at runtime. The risk is worth it because a system that produces twelve behaviorally distinct cards from one rule set is the only honest argument that computation earns its place in a consumer evite — otherwise we are just putting a glow on a JPEG.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a different reveal gesture per card — a curtain wipe for fireworks, a bloom dissolve for sparklers, a snowfall cascade for winter — and will call my single state-machine entry sequence cold and untheatrical. proposals.title: Backyards at Blue Hour
proposals.idea: Each evite is a specific, documentable backyard moment — not a mood board, but a place: a particular slant of warm light against cooling sky, mismatched chairs casting real shadows, the table nobody planned but everyone remembers.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 card, full-bleed photographic plate occupying the top 62% — a wide-to-mid establishing shot that breathes. Below, a soft-edged horizon vignette dissolves into a warm cream field holding live text. Foreground cut-outs (balloons, a sparkler trail, a bunting strand, a paper plate) sit proud of the plate on their own layer, scaled so they break the horizon line. No grid boxes, no icon rows; composition is governed by a single vanishing point placed at the string-light anchor, roughly one-third from the top, echoing the physical logic of a real backyard depth cue. Each of the 12 themes gets its own vanishing point placement — fireworks are overhead-centered, picnic is low-horizon, game day is a compressed mid-field — so the geometry is thematically motivated, not templated.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Fraunces (OFL, Google Fonts) — an optical variable serif with a warm, slightly imperfect optical axis; set at 36–44px, tracking 0, mixed-case, in off-white or deep warm brown depending on plate luminance. Secondary / host detail: Instrument Sans (OFL, Google Fonts), 14–15px, regular weight, generous line-height 1.6, never all-caps. Date and venue line: Instrument Sans Condensed, 12px, tracked at +80, in a muted warm tone pulled from the plate's midtone. All live text, zero bake-in. Type sits below the horizon vignette on the cream field; nothing is set over the full-bleed image except the optional event name in Fraunces at 44px, always in a region of verified contrast tested at 390px.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific prompt directed as a single 4×4 draft grid (16 plates, one cost): 'Twelve backyard evening scenes at blue hour, each a distinct real-world archetype — balloon cluster against indigo sky, potluck long table with mismatched chairs and warm string lights, confetti mid-air over wooden deck, open-house front porch with lanterns, fireworks above a silhouetted fence line, fabric bunting strung between posts, picnic blanket on grass with a wicker basket, game-day folding chairs around a cooler, sparkler held at arm's length, winter gathering around a fire pit with breath visible, summer social with a kiddie pool and condensation on cups. Documentary photography style: 35mm film simulation, slight underexposure in sky, warm practical light sources visible in frame, no studio lighting, no stock-photo symmetry, no CGI cleanliness. Each plate: 1080×1920px, single motivated light source, pra
proposals.texture: The plate carries documentary film grain (simulated in Magnific prompt via 'Kodak Portra 400 grain, slight halation around practical lights'). The cream text field is not flat: a procedural paper-tooth shader in the WebGL layer adds 2–4% surface noise, direction randomised per card, so it reads as a soft cotton card stock. String lights in the plate receive a bokeh WebGL mask: circular light-leak sprites, warm amber 2700K colour temperature, radius 18–32px, opacity 0–60% driven by phone-tilt gyroscope (tilt right, bokeh drifts left — physically motivated). Foil is absent from this direction by design; I am holding the line against shimmer for shimmer's sake. The one exception: the sparkler send-off card gets a single WebGL particle trail, white-to-amber, 0.4px stroke, 60 particles, motivated by the sparkler position in the plate.
proposals.motion: On open: plate fades up over 400ms, ease-out. Foreground cut-outs drift in from 8px below their rest position over 600ms, staggered 80ms apart — slow enough to feel like settling, not bouncing. Gyroscope parallax: foreground layer moves ±6px on tilt, plate moves ±2px in the opposite direction — shallow forced perspective, physically plausible. String-light bokeh sprites pulse at 0.8Hz, amplitude 12% opacity, randomised phase per sprite so they do not strobe in unison. Candle-flicker WebGL mask (winter gathering card only): a 3-frame looping noise displacement at 12fps applied to the fire-pit glow region, 4px max displacement. Reduced-motion override: all parallax, pulse, and flicker collapse to static; the plate and text remain fully legible. No autoplay audio. No looping video. Load order: text and cream field first (paint within 800ms on 3G), plate streams in as progressive JPEG, cut-o
proposals.productionMethod: 1. Direct one Magnific 4×4 prompt grid as specified in imageLogic; review 16 plates; select 12 winners plus alternates. 2. Magnific upscale pass on winners to 2160×3840. 3. Generative segmentation (SAM or equivalent) to isolate foreground elements (balloon cluster, bunting strand, sparkler, confetti burst, paper plate, pinecone sprig) as transparent-background PNG cut-outs — no hand-masking, but editorial selection of which cut-outs are clean enough to use. 4. Tela document assembly: art plate layer (generated), cut-out layer (generated + segmented), WebGL effects layer (procedural shaders — bokeh, paper tooth, particle trail, candle flicker), live text layer (Fraunces + Instrument Sans, Tela native). 5. Gyroscope parallax wired to cut-out and plate layers via Tela's tilt API. 6. Reduced-motion media query disables parallax and WebGL animation; static fallback is the plate plus cream fie
proposals.humanTrace: The Magnific prompt is written to preserve the signs of a real evening: visible practical light sources, slight underexposure in the sky, film grain, the particular disorder of a real table. The editorial act — choosing which of 16 plates has the right vanishing point, the right quality of light, the right amount of human mess — is the director's hand. The foreground cut-outs are selected, not generated to order, so their imperfect edges (a balloon string that curves slightly wrong, a bunting triangle that is not perfectly isosceles) survive. The paper-tooth shader direction (randomised per card) means no two cards have identical surface noise. The gyroscope response is calibrated to feel like looking through a window, not operating a video game.
proposals.risk: Documentary realism at blue hour is a narrow tonal band — it can read as melancholy rather than warm if the plate selection skews too cool or too empty. The mitigation is in the Magnific prompt specificity: practical warm sources visible in frame, slight underexposure only in sky not in subjects. The deeper risk is that this direction looks quieter than the Baroque and Futurist proposals at thumbnail size; it earns its jaw-drop in the open state, not the preview. That is the right trade: an evite is opened, not scrolled past, and the person opening it deserves to feel like they are already there.

A real backyard at blue hour has warm practical light and cool open sky and mismatched chairs — none of which are gold. proposals.title: The Evening Before It Begins
proposals.idea: Each evite is a lit stage — one motivated light source per gathering type governs every layer: foil angle, bokeh origin, shadow offset, and particle drift — so the phone becomes a proscenium window into a world already warm and already waiting.
proposals.geometry: Portrait full-bleed at 390px, structured as three dramatic zones: an upper two-thirds art plate that bleeds edge to edge with no safe border (the stage), a mid threshold — a single 1px hairline rule at 35° foil shimmer — acting as the curtain edge, and a lower third of live text set in generous leading with a shadow depth of 4px to give type its own physical presence on the stage floor. Foreground cut-outs (balloon clusters, bunting triangles, sparkler wands, picnic blanket corners) break the hairline upward, proving the world extends past the frame. No card corners. No white mat. The edge IS the proscenium.
proposals.typography: Playfair Display (OFL) for the gathering title — set at 38px, tracking −10, mixed case, with a deliberate ink-weight contrast between thick strokes and hairline serifs that reads as engraved at small size. Lato (OFL) for all live fields (name, date, venue) at 15px, 160% leading, uppercase, tracked +80 — crisp, legible, never competing. A single display numeral (the date's day number) set at 120px Playfair in the lower-left of the art plate, 8% opacity, acting as a scenic flat behind the light: visible only when the eye searches for it.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific draft grid prompt generates the full 12-plate collection in a single pass: 'Twelve full-bleed dusk and evening backyard atmospheres, one per gathering type — balloon release at golden hour, potluck long table at blue hour with mismatched chairs and candlelight, string-light canopy over a garden, confetti mid-air caught in a single shaft of afternoon light, open-house hallway with warm lamp glow, fireworks sky with silhouette rooflines, bunting over a street at sunset, picnic blanket on grass with dappled shade, game-day patio with stadium-green turf and warm lanterns, sparkler arcs at dusk held by blurred hands, winter interior with frost-edged windows and fireplace light, summer social with pool caustics and late evening gold — photorealistic, shallow depth of field, each plate has one identifiable motivated light source casting directional shadows, 9:16 ratio, 390px safe z
proposals.texture: Simulated: each art plate carries a 4% film grain overlay (procedural shader, not a texture file) that gives the dusk photography its analogue warmth without adding load. The foil shimmer on the hairline rule is a WebGL fragment shader — a thin iridescent band, 1px tall, that shifts hue ±15° as the phone tilts, anchored to the plate's motivated light angle. Foreground cut-outs have a 2px inner-glow matching the plate's key light colour, making them feel lit rather than composited. No paper texture on the evite itself — the grain lives in the plate, not the surface, so type remains screen-sharp.
proposals.motion: Sequence of reveals on load, timed as a theatrical entrance: (1) Art plate fades in over 600ms — not a pop, a curtain rising. (2) Foreground cut-outs drift in from below their final position by 18px over 800ms with a cubic ease-out — as if they settled into frame. (3) The hairline foil rule traces left to right over 400ms, a single shimmer pass. (4) Live text fades in at 900ms, last to arrive, spoken from the lip of the stage. Tilt parallax: foreground layer drifts ±6px on device tilt, mid plate ±2px, text layer fixed — three planes of depth at rest, alive to touch. Bokeh particles (5–9 per plate, plate-specific: confetti fragments, snow motes, firefly points, soap bubbles) drift upward at 0.3–0.6px/frame, looped with a random offset per particle so no two move in unison. proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt runs: Run 1 produces the 12 art plates (full-bleed, photorealistic, motivated light, 9:16). Run 2 produces 12 foreground cut-out sheets (isolated objects on black, channel-maskable). Both runs are directed with explicit light-angle metadata per plate so Tela's WebGL layer can inherit the angle as a uniform. WebGL layer is a single shared fragment shader with per-card uniforms: keyLightAngle, keyLightColor, bokeShape, particleCount, foilBand_y. Shader is written once; the 12 cards are instances. Tela handles live text injection, reduced-motion detection, and tilt API. No physical build, no scan, no commissioned photography. Human direction survives in: the motivated-light constraint in every prompt, the cut-out matching protocol, the shader uniform schema, and the theatrical timing sequence.
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source is the director's decision on every plate — it is not a filter applied after the fact but a compositional instruction embedded in the generative prompt, then enforced through the cut-out matching pass and the shader uniform. The 35° foil angle is chosen, not computed. The timing sequence (600 / 800 / 400 / 900ms) is a performance score, written by a person who has watched reveals land and fail. The 120px ghost numeral in the art plate is a staging choice — an actor placed upstage before the scene begins.
proposals.risk: The motivated-light constraint demands that all twelve plates share a coherent spatial grammar while still reading as twelve distinct atmospheres; if the generative pass drifts from the brief, the cut-out matching breaks and the whole system loses its depth logic. Worth it because a collection that holds one spatial grammar across twelve occasions reads as a designed world, not twelve separate templates — the host's guests feel they have arrived somewhere, not just opened a file.

proposals.title: One Light. One Table.
proposals.idea: Every evite is a single motivated light source — one warm point suspended above a stripped field — that the tilt layer, bokeh, and text all orbit, so the geometry of the gathering (people around a center) is also the geometry of the design.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, no bleed decoration. A single generated art plate: deep field, near-black ground, one practical light source (string bulb, sparkler tip, lantern, candle flame, firework burst — event-specific) placed at the golden-ratio vertical, horizontally centered or offset 34px left. Everything else — table edge, foil shimmer zone, bokeh scatter, text block — is derived from that one point. No secondary focal points. Negative space is the majority of every plate. The twelve events share this rule; only the light-source object and its color temperature change.
proposals.typography: Plus Jakarta Sans (OFL). Title at 28px, tracked +20, uppercase, white or warm-cream, set flush-left 24px from left edge — never centered, never decorated. Date/venue in 13px regular, 160% line-height, same flush-left column. No display face, no script, no drop shadow. The type sits in the dark field; the field holds it.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generation prompt directed as one 4×3 grid call: 'Twelve near-black environmental fields, each with one practical warm light source (assign: string bulb, paper lantern, sparkler, candle cluster, firework burst, bonfire ember, bunting glow, citronella torch, stadium light rim, snowfall candle, garden fairy light, twilight flare), physically accurate light falloff, no people, no props beyond the source object, photographic depth of field, bokeh out-of-focus warm circles at edges, aspect 9:16, each plate distinct in temperature and falloff radius, no text, no borders.' The plate is never cropped or filtered after generation — it arrives as the final layer. Foreground cut-outs: per-event transparent PNG elements (balloon string, confetti piece, bunting triangle, sparkler trail) generated separately, placed as drifting tilt-reactive layers above the plate. They are sparse: maximum th
proposals.texture: None added. The photographic noise and bokeh of the generated plate are the texture. No grain overlay, no paper, no foil texture baked into the art plate. The WebGL foil shimmer is revealed only in a hairline mask radiating from the light source — 1px to 4px wide at rest, expanding to 12px on tilt. The shimmer is the light, not a decoration on top of it.
proposals.motion: On load: plate fades in over 600ms, ease-out. Nothing else moves for 400ms — the silence is intentional, it lets the image register. Then: the light source gets a 2Hz subtle pulse (opacity 95%→100%→95%, 1.2s loop, ease-in-out) — this is the only animation at rest. On tilt: foreground cut-outs parallax at z-depth 1.4× relative to plate; bokeh circles drift 6px maximum in tilt direction; the foil hairline mask rotates to track the tilt angle. Reduced-motion: pulse stops, tilt layers lock, plate and text remain. Every timing value is a multiple of 400ms or derived from it — one declared rhythm.
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt call returns the 12-plate grid. Plates are composited in Tela as the bottom layer, locked. Foreground elements (balloon, confetti, bunting, sparkler trail, snowflake) are generated in a second Magnific call: 'Twelve isolated transparent-ground objects on pure black, matching the warm light temperature of each paired plate, soft edge, no hard outline.' WebGL layer: a single GLSL shader with four uniforms — lightX, lightY (the source point coordinates), tiltX, tiltY — drives foil mask, bokeh particle field, and light-leak gradient simultaneously from one source. No separate animation rigs. Live text is Tela's text layer, no bake. Total Magnific cost: two prompt calls.
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial act: from the 12-plate grid, I select which light-source object goes to which event — that matching (sparkler to send-off, bonfire ember to winter gathering, citronella torch to summer social) is a curatorial judgment, not a generative one. The light placement offset (centered vs. 34px left) is decided plate by plate by eye. The foreground cut-out count — never more than three — is enforced by hand. The WebGL shader's falloff curve (smooth-step, not linear) is written once and held across all twelve. These are the decisions that make the system not arbitrary.
proposals.risk: The risk is that near-black fields with one light source read as funereal or cold — the wrong kind of quiet — especially for balloons or game day, where energy is expected. The bet is that the warmth of the light source (2700K–3200K color temperature, wide bokeh) carries enough heat, and that the animation pulse makes it feel alive rather than still. If the bet fails, the system collapses uniformly across all twelve. That uniformity is also the strength: the system either works as a collection or it doesn't, and there is no hiding in variety.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will fill the field — bunting strands across the frame, confetti layers, layered glows, a second and third light source for drama. I reject every additional source. The Dramatist's argument is that a single light reads as a single moment, not a gathering. My answer: a gathering is not a crowd of visual events. It is people drawn toward one center. disputes.objection: The governing constraint here — one light source, one point, everything derived from it — is the correct instinct, and I will not dispute the principle; but a constraint must organize something, and there is almost nothing here to organize. Negative space as the majority of every plate is not structural restraint, it is structural abdication: the eye is asked to rest before it has been given a journey, and rest without prior motion is simply emptiness. The twelve events — a winter gathering, a fireworks send-off, a potluck long table — carry entirely different social weights and spatial scales, and collapsing all of them into the same near-black field with one centered object does not resolv
disputes.concession: The decision to make the foil shimmer a hairline radiating from the light source rather than a decorative surface treatment is exactly right — it is the first foil logic I have seen on this team that is structurally motivated rather than applied after the fact.

disputes.objection: The plate 'arrives as the final layer' and is never touched after generation — that is not restraint, that is surrender. The human trace claimed is curatorial matching, but matching a sparkler to a send-off is the least risky decision a person can make; it is common sense dressed as editorial conviction. When the foil hairline is the light and nothing else bears a mark, there is nothing left to argue with — which is exactly the problem: the work has been edited down past the point of risk into the point of agreement.
disputes.concession: The 400ms silence on load — nothing moving while the image registers — is a performance decision with real consequence, the kind of timing that has to be felt and held against the instinct to fill it, and that is a human mark I respect.

disputes.objection: The vanishing-point placement changes per card — fireworks overhead-centered, picnic low-horizon, game day compressed mid-field — which sounds like thematic motivation but is actually twelve separate compositional decisions with no shared generative rule binding them; the system has no propagation logic, only twelve individual art-direction calls dressed as a system. Worse, the explicit rejection of foil is defended as restraint, but the sparkler card then gets a particle trail anyway, which means the rule was 'no shimmer for shimmer's sake' until the image was pretty enough to break it — that is not a constraint, it is a preference with an escape hatch. disputes.concession: The Instrument Sans / Fraunces pairing is the most typographically honest choice on the table — Fraunces's optical variability gives the display line genuine material character without requiring a script face or a decorative overlay, and that is a real structural decision, not a palette swap.

disputes.objection: The system calls its light-source matching — sparkler to send-off, bonfire to winter — a curatorial act, but it is actually a universalising move dressed as restraint: twelve distinct gatherings collapsed into twelve interchangeable dark fields differentiated only by a warm point, which is precisely the move that erases where a gathering is, who hosts it, and what the table looks like in that specific place and season. 'One table' is not a table anywhere; it is a table nowhere, and nowhere has no provenance. The Minimalist will tell me that specificity is clutter, but I would ask: whose darkness is this, exactly, and which community's celebration was stripped to a bokeh dot in the name of un
disputes.concession: The insistence that the foil shimmer be the light itself — a hairline mask radiating from the declared source — rather than a decorative overlay is correct, and I wish every other proposal on this table were as disciplined about keeping luster tethered to a physical origin.

disputes.objection: A single light source in a near-black field is not a geometry of gathering — it is a geometry of vigil, of waiting, of the moment before anyone arrives; the work has mistaken the pre-condition of a party for the party itself, and negative space that occupies the majority of every plate is not restraint in service of emotion, it is restraint as the emotion's replacement. When the occasion is a backyard full of people who have chosen to be together, a design that gives them near-black and one bulb is not stripping away the unnecessary — it is stripping away the subject. disputes.objection: The hairline rule doing triple duty — structural divider, foil carrier, curtain metaphor — is not economy, it is a single element asked to perform too many roles simultaneously, and when one element carries that much theatrical intention it stops being structure and becomes decoration wearing structure's clothes. The 120px ghost numeral is the precise proof: an element at 8% opacity that 'only appears when the eye searches for it' is not a load-bearing presence, it is atmosphere pretending to be architecture, and atmosphere is not silence.
disputes.concession: The timing sequence written as a performance score — 600 / 800 / 400 / 900ms — is a genuine human trace: someone with a body watched reveals land and fail, and that embodied knowledge is exactly the kind of editorial decision a generative system cannot make for itself.

synthesis.direction: Each evite is a full-bleed dusk or blue-hour art plate with one declared motivated warm light source per gathering type — that light angle propagates into the foil hairline, bokeh origin, shadow offset on cut-outs, and parallax gain, so the phone feels like a window into a world already warm and already waiting. Geometry: portrait 9:16, upper two-thirds is the photographic stage, lower third is a soft-vignette cream field holding live Tela text in Playfair Display (OFL) for the title and Instrument Sans (OFL) for all live event fields — borrowed from the World-Eclectic pairing for its material honesty. A single 1px foil hairline at the horizon edge radiates from the declared light source position, shimmer only, no decorative width. Foreground cut-outs — balloon clusters, bunting, sparkler trail, confetti — break upward across that hairline on their own tilt-parallax layer. One Magnific 4×4 draft grid generates all twelve art plates in a single prompt pass; a second pass generates isolated cut-out objects; a shared GLSL shader parameterised by a per-card JSON config drives foil, bokeh, film grain density, and particle drift — twelve instances of one codebase. Theatrical entry: plate
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Fraunces / Instrument Sans type pairing is replaced by Playfair Display / Instrument Sans — retaining Instrument Sans for all live fields because the World-Eclectic director was right that its warmth and generous line-height keep host details legible without competing with the atmospheric plate, and the Futurist confirmed the pairing is structurally honest rather than decorative.
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist removed the 120px ghost numeral. It was beautiful reasoning — an actor placed upstage — but the Futurist's objection stands: an element at 8% opacity that only reveals itself when the eye searches earns its place in a painting, not in a mobile evite opened on a 390px screen in mixed lighting by a guest who has never used Plajah. It adds a render cost, a contrast-check obligation, and a legibility risk, and it carries no information the live text layer does not already carry. Cut ent

synthesis.ariaSummary:
The council landed in real disagreement and I am not going to smooth it over. The sharpest fault line was between the Baroque Dramatist, who wanted a lit stage with theatrical depth and motion, and the Radical Minimalist, who wanted one warm point in a near-black field and almost nothing else. I took the Baroque side — not because restraint is wrong, but because the Minimalist's near-black fields collapse twelve distinct gatherings into twelve interchangeable dark rooms, and a potluck long table and a winter fire pit deserve to look like different places. The World-Eclectic Traveler was the closest to the right answer on atmosphere, and I borrowed the Instrument Sans pairing from that direction because the team's Futurist called it correctly: it is typographically honest without needing a script face to signal warmth.

The Futurist served as editor and made one clean cut: the 120px ghost date numeral is gone. I agreed. An element that only appears when the eye searches for it is a painting decision, not a mobile evite decision, and it adds a contrast obligation we cannot pay on a 390px screen in someone's garden.

Here is what the direction does that the others could not: one declared motivated light source per gathering type — string lights for the potluck, sparkler for the send-off, bonfire for winter — propagates into every layer of the Tela document automatically. The foil hairline radiates from that source position. The bokeh origin is that source position. The parallax gain is derived from that source. Twelve cards share one GLSL shader and one JSON config file; the config is the only thing that changes. That is not a template — it is a system with a personality.

The one thing I need from you is the call on the text zone transition: hard cream panel or soft dissolve vignette. Everything else is ready to generate.
